analysis.session_summary: BOJ policy headlines dominated Asia and London, with the yen the weakest major at -0.514% despite an in-line rate hike, while CHF led gains at +0.32% and GBP followed at +0.312% after a strong UK retail sales beat. Equities slipped and VIX rose 0.85%, keeping the tape defensive. Most major legs lacked clear catalysts, with only partial attribution to BOJ, Ueda, and Lagarde remarks.

themes.theme: BOJ-driven JPY weakness despite in-line hike
themes.evidence: BOJ Policy Rate +1 more printed inline but JPY own impulse was -0.193%; USD/JPY closed +73.8 pips at 156.793; CHF/JPY closed +138.7 pips at 190.623; JPY mean -0.514% vs majors.
CHF mean +0.32% vs majors; USD/CHF closed -21.2 pips at 0.82276, close at 0.06 of its 34.0 pip range; EUR/CHF closed -26.4 pips at 0.944, close at 0.01 of its 36.9 pip range.
Retail Sales m/m actual 0.5% vs forecast -0.2% triggered GBP strength of 0.042%; GBP mean +0.312%; GBP/USD +33.6 pips close 1.33822; EUR/GBP -23.5 pips close 0.85735.

themes.theme: Risk cautious with equity dip and energy volatility
themes.evidence: SPX -13.5 points, VIX +0.848%, Brent/USD -90.8 pips (-0.855%) after Saudi oil supply headline; USD/MXN +457.0 pips.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD chopped through five legs (15.4 up, -12.0 down, 10.4 up, -31.9 down, 16.3 up) with no single catalyst, although BOJ-related flow contributed to early gains and only weak attribution to Lagarde and Industrial Production.

polarity_reads.read: Inline rate hike but JPY still fell 0.193%, suggesting the market wanted more hawkish guidance; positioning leans short JPY or long carry.
JPY strengthened 0.204% with no forecast to score; likely position squaring after Ueda comments, not a clear hawkish shift.
AUD strengthened 0.067% with no forecast; stable labour market comments offered mild support without a tradable surprise.
Clear beat surprise (0.5% vs -0.2%) lifted GBP 0.042%; confirms positive GBP momentum and supports long GBP against EUR.
Muted -0.038% inside the noise floor; no new EUR impulse, so EUR crosses remain flow-driven.
